content.comment_body: Can anyone help explain the logic shown in the attached image? Specifically: The counter [article_no] only increases when output Q2 is 0 and Q3 is 1. Q3 controls the Q2 relay, so Q3's status should be processed before Q2's relay logic. If Q3 is 1, this feeds into an OR instruction before the Q2 relay, meaning that Q2 should not be set to 0 by the logic when Q3 is 1. The software environment used is [product_name] Demo [version_no] running in simulation mode. More details about this application are available at [url].
Please upload your program as a ZIP file. The provided link directs to a site that requires login credentials.

Outputs and flags experience a one-cycle delay between input and output in this setup. Your screenshot shows the input to Q3 is high while the output is still low, then updates high in the following cycle. In my picture, all outputs are wired in series with a 'Not' gate ahead; the simulator's slower cycling lets you observe this behavior. Actual hardware operates faster, but the logic behaves the same.
To verify program behavior in simulation mode, pause execution and click the green button with your mouse. Advancing one cycle at a time lets you see if the order matches your expectations.

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced unexpected simulation timing in [product_name], with relay output logic not updating as anticipated. Community members explained this is due to inherent one-cycle delays in output and flag updates within the software, a characteristic particularly visible during simulation.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipated that relay coil logic would result in immediate, sequential output updates within the same simulation cycle, without any unexplained delay.
